name: the natures
roots: nature (Latin natura, from nasci, to be born: what a being is by its birth); here the register a being is in — a body, or the sayable

name: body
roots: σῶμα (the law's word); body (Old English bodig: the trunk, the frame); what takes room in space

name: the sayable
roots: λεκτόν (the law's word); say (Old English secgan); what is placed in an order — a register, a habitat — and takes no room

name: nature
roots: natura (from nasci, to be born); which of the two natures a being is in

name: kind
roots: γένος (the law's word); kind (Old English cynd: birth, lineage — kin): a line of beings that come to be alike

name: the kinds
roots: γένη (the plural of γένος: the law's registry of kinds)

name: the lines
roots: line (linea: a linen thread): the ladder's strands, each a way beings stand on one another

name: frame
roots: frame (Old English framian: to be of use, to make ready — a structure that holds): space∞time, what every body stands on

name: matter
roots: materia (timber, stuff): the body's dot and what it binds into

name: gravitation
roots: gravis (heavy): matter organised by its weight — where direction begins, and the larger holds the smaller in its path

name: the living
roots: life (Old English līf): possible on a world in balance, and given along the life chain

name: reason
roots: λόγος (the law's word, from λέγω: to gather, to lay in order, to say); reason (ratio: a reckoning, and a proportion — the two senses the ladder parts); the line on which the sayable stands

name: the made
roots: make (Old English macian: to fit together): made on purpose, through hands

name: conditions
roots: condicio (a stipulation: con + dicere, to say together): what a step stands on while it holds

name: balance
roots: bilanx (having two scales: bi + lanx, a dish): the mean — a steady state within the bounds a life keeps, never equilibrium, which is rest

name: proportion
roots: pro portione (according to each part's share): ratio in its second sense, on which reason is possible

name: rules of foundation
roots: found (fundare: to lay the bottom, fundus): what holds for everything standing on a step

name: weight
roots: weight (Old English wiht, from wegan, to carry — kin to weigh and way): every body has weight, standing on space∞time; a sayable being has none of its own

name: the order of bodies
roots: order (Latin ordo: a row of threads in a loom, a rank); complexity (com-plectere, to braid together): each level braided of the one it stands on

name: space∞time
roots: space (spatium: a stretch) and time (a span): one structure with two faces; Minkowski, 1908: space by itself and time by itself fade into shadows, and only a union of the two keeps a reality of its own

name: force field
roots: force (Latin fortis, strong); field (Old English feld, open land) — Faraday's lines of force: a field that binds or gives mass, filling room without excluding

name: matter field
roots: matter (materia, the stuff a thing is made of, from mater); field — a field that takes room and excludes, its quanta the quarks and leptons

name: elementary particle
roots: element (Latin elementum: a first principle; a letter of the alphabet); particle (particula: a little part); the dot of matter: what has no part known today

name: hadron
roots: ἁδρός (thick, stout, full-grown): particles bound of quarks, named so in 1962

name: nucleus
roots: nucleus (Latin: a kernel, from nux, a nut): the core of an atom

name: atom
roots: ἄτομος (uncut, indivisible) — the name kept when the atom was found divisible, as every dot found divisible keeps its system

name: molecule
roots: molecula (New Latin: a little mass, from moles, a mass, a heap)

name: cell
roots: cella (Latin: a small room, a store-chamber) — Hooke, 1665, saw cork's little rooms

name: tissue
roots: tissu (Old French: woven, from texere, to weave): cells of one kind woven as one

name: organ
roots: ὄργανον (a tool, from ἔργον, work) — yet it is the capacity that has organs, not the organ capacities (Heidegger, 1929/30): a part serving a capacity of the whole

name: organism
roots: ὄργανον via French organisme: a whole of organs that is one being — a microbe, a tree, an animal, a person

name: population
roots: populus (a people): organisms of one kind living together — a herd, a stand of trees

name: community
roots: communis (shared: com + munus, a duty or gift held in common): populations of many kinds living together

name: ecosystem
roots: οἶκος (a house, a household) + σύστημα: a community with the matter it lives on and in (Tansley, 1935)

name: reason
roots: λόγος (the law's word, from λέγω: to gather, to lay in order, to say); reason (ratio: a reckoning, and a proportion — the two senses the ladder parts); possible on living organisation while its proportion holds — no body stands here

name: material
roots: materia (timber, the hard wood of a tree, from mater, mother: the trunk that bears the shoots): matter in bulk

name: celestial body
roots: caelum (the sky): a body of the sky — a planet, a moon

name: planetary system
roots: πλανήτης (a wanderer): bodies held in paths about the largest among them

name: galaxy
roots: γάλα (milk): ὁ γαλαξίας κύκλος, the milky circle

name: component
roots: componere (to put together): a made part — a chip, a board, a cable

name: device
roots: devis (Old French: a design, a division, from dividere) — what it does beyond keeping its form is lent it by its makers and keepers

name: the crown
roots: corona (a wreath, from κορώνη, anything curved): where every chain ends — one, `theone`, with two faces, love and wisdom

name: the Necessary Existent
roots: THE ONE (the law's code, `theone`); necessary (necesse: ne + cedere, what cannot give way — what cannot not be); Ibn Sina's واجب الوجود, the one whose being is by itself: the end of every chain, named on no bean

name: love
roots: ἀγάπη: love that does not possess — the face of the crown by which every life is given; a person is held by it, and by no bean

name: wisdom
roots: wise (Old English wīs, from a root meaning to see, to know — kin to wit and vision); σοφία: the face by which what is, is known

name: via
roots: via (Latin: by the way of): through whom this came to be — born of, made by, said by; every chain ends at the Creator, whom no bean names

name: status
roots: status (Latin: a standing, from stare, to stand): where a being stands on its kind's lifecycle

name: dimensions
roots: dimension (dimetiri, to measure out): time and length the frame, mass, information, money, temperature

name: time
roots: time (Old English tīma: a span — from a root that means to divide, as tide): with length, the frame the universe is divided in, neither prior

name: length
roots: long (Old English lang): how far — with time, the frame, neither prior

name: when
roots: when (Old English hwænne); Aristotle's category πότε — a position on the one line everything that happens is ordered along

name: where
roots: where (Old English hwǣr); Aristotle's category ποῦ — a position among the places a being can be

name: complements
roots: complere (to fill up): how a position in place finds its time, and a position in time its place

name: stated
roots: state (from status: to set down): the entry says its other half itself

name: the bearer's
roots: bear (Old English beran, to carry): else its other half is the bearer's

name: the system's
roots: σύστημα (what stands together): the system carries its other half itself

name: division
roots: dividere (to part): a dot is without parts in its own system; what is divided keeps its system and its wholeness

name: divisions
roots: dividere (to part): each whole, its parts and their wholeness, with the rule that judges it

name: part of
roots: pars (a part); whole (Old English hāl: sound, entire — kin to heal and holy): a being is part of at most one whole

name: lives in
roots: live (Old English libban: to live, to remain): the habitat a being lives in or on

name: located at
roots: locus (a place): where a being is, a position in each system it is found in

name: owner
roots: own (Old English āgan: to have, to possess): whose a being is — one owner, and no facets; the ways of caring for it are who answers for it

name: answers for
roots: respondere (to promise in return: re + spondere, to pledge): who answers for a being, facet by facet

name: acquired from
roots: acquire (acquirere: ad + quaerere, to seek): from whom a being came to us — not how it came to be, and not whose it is

name: facets of care
roots: facet (facette: a little face); care (Old English caru: concern — Heidegger's Sorge): the ways of answering for a being, never of owning it

name: legal
roots: lex (law): who answers for a being before the law — its owner, unless the owner is outside or no bean

name: technical
roots: τέχνη (craft): who runs and maintains a being — care for its working; only a being that runs or is kept has one

name: experience
roots: experiri (to try, to go through): who answers for how people meet a being

name: financial
roots: finis (an end: a settlement that ends a debt): who pays for a being and is paid by it

name: acts
roots: actum (a thing done, from agere, to drive, to do): how a value came to be where it is

name: made
roots: make (Old English macian: to fit together): made here, from nothing given

name: derived
roots: derivare (to lead water off a stream: de + rivus): it holds nothing its source did not

name: read
roots: read (Old English rǣdan: to advise, to interpret, to read): read off the world or a clock

name: said
roots: say (Old English secgan): said by someone, or stated in a document

name: provenance
roots: provenire (to come forth): who said it, how they know, and as of when

name: layers
roots: lay (Old English lecgan: to lay down): each layer rests on the one beneath

name: manifesto
roots: manifestus (plain, evident — perhaps struck by the hand): what daftar holds to, one clause to a sentence

name: law
roots: law (Old Norse lagu: what is laid down): what is in force, in the present tense, applied alone

name: reasoning
roots: ratio (a reckoning, from reri, to reckon): why a law is as it is, keyed by the item it supports

name: journal
roots: diurnalis (daily, from dies, a day): what was done and why, entry by entry, appended and never rewritten

name: history
roots: ἱστορία (an inquiry: knowing by having seen — ἵστωρ, a witness): the exact record, never summarised

name: queue
roots: cauda (a tail): what waits for a person — proposed, parked, settled

name: names
roots: name (Old English nama; ὄνομα): the law's words in its readers' languages, siblings, for publication — never read for meaning

name: view
roots: videre (to see): a page of drawings — what it draws, the lenses it is read at, where it is shown

name: lenses
roots: lens (Latin: a lentil — the glass is shaped like one): the four depths a drawing is read at

name: orient
roots: oriens (the rising: the east, where the sun rises; to orient is to find it): what a drawn thing is for, to one who has never touched it

name: understand
roots: understandan (to stand among: to grasp from within): how the parts co-operate, where the work is decided

name: operate
roots: operari (to work, from opus): what the person on call must know first, now

name: inspect
roots: inspicere (to look into): what exactly the parts are and how that is known

name: garden
roots: garden (Frankish *gardo: an enclosure; kin to yard): a repository of beans, stating itself in GARDEN.md; paradise (Avestan pairi-daēza: walled around)

name: a name
roots: name (Old English nama): a row of a names file — an item of the law named in one language, with its roots
